CLINICAL GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Children's Hospital
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
Age: 3 years
Sex: Female
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

REFERRING PHYSICIAN
[redacted name], MD
Pediatric Neurology

CLINICAL INDICATION
3-year-old female presenting with developmental regression, loss of purposeful hand skills, stereotypic hand movements, and acquired microcephaly. Clinical suspicion of Rett syndrome.

CLINICAL HISTORY
The patient had normal development until approximately 18 months of age, when parents noted gradual loss of acquired language skills and purposeful hand use. She subsequently developed repetitive hand-wringing movements. Head circumference, which was at the 50th percentile at birth, has decelerated and is now below the 3rd percentile. No family history of neurodevelopmental disorders reported.

TEST PERFORMED
Whole Exome Sequencing - Trio Analysis
• Proband and biological parents analyzed
• Library preparation: Agilent SureSelect Human All Exon V7
• Sequencing platform: Illumina NovaSeq 6000
• Mean coverage: 120x (proband), 100x (parents)
• Minimum coverage threshold: 20x for >95% of coding regions
• Analysis focused on genes associated with neurodevelopmental disorders

TECHNICAL FINDINGS

MECP2 (NM_004992.3): c.808C>T p.(Arg270*)
• Heterozygous nonsense variant detected in proband
• Coverage at variant position: 142x
• Variant allele frequency: 48%
• Not detected in either parent (coverage: Mother 98x, Father 102x)
• De novo status confirmed

VARIANT CLASSIFICATION
The MECP2 c.808C>T p.(Arg270*) variant is classified as PATHOGENIC (Class 5) based on:
• PVS1: Nonsense variant in gene where loss-of-function is known disease mechanism
• PS2: De novo occurrence confirmed by trio analysis
• PM2: Absent from population databases (gnomAD)
• PP5: Multiple reputable sources classify as pathogenic (ClinVar consensus)

CLINICAL INTERPRETATION
The identified de novo nonsense variant in MECP2 confirms the clinical diagnosis of Rett syndrome (OMIM #312750). The p.Arg270* variant is one of the most common pathogenic variants in MECP2, accounting for approximately 6% of classic Rett syndrome cases. This variant results in premature protein truncation, eliminating critical functional domains including the transcriptional repression domain.

Patients with the p.Arg270* variant typically present with classic Rett syndrome phenotype, including:
• Normal early development followed by regression (6-18 months)
• Loss of purposeful hand skills with stereotypic movements
• Acquired microcephaly
• Gait abnormalities
• Variable seizure onset (typically after 4 years)

DEVELOPMENTAL PREDICTIONS
Based on genotype-phenotype correlations for p.Arg270*:
• Regression phase expected to stabilize by age 4-5 years
• Ambulation may be preserved in 50% of cases
• Communication skills typically limited to eye gaze
• Seizures develop in approximately 70% by adolescence
• Scoliosis risk increases after age 8

CLINICAL MANAGEMENT RECOMMENDATIONS

1. MULTIDISCIPLINARY CARE COORDINATION
   • Pediatric neurology for seizure monitoring and management
   • Physical therapy for motor function preservation
   • Occupational therapy for hand function and daily activities
   • Speech/communication therapy with augmentative communication devices
   • Developmental pediatrics for comprehensive care coordination

2. SURVEILLANCE
   • EEG monitoring annually or with clinical changes
   • Orthopedic evaluation for scoliosis screening (annually after age 5)
   • Nutritional assessment and growth monitoring
   • Cardiac evaluation including QTc monitoring
   • Sleep study if breathing irregularities develop

3. SUPPORTIVE INTERVENTIONS
   • Consider trial of communication devices/eye gaze technology
   • Nutritional support as needed for growth failure
   • Constipation management
   • Bone health monitoring

4. GENETIC COUNSELING
   • Recurrence risk for parents: ~1% due to theoretical germline mosaicism
   • Future prenatal testing available
   • X-linked dominant inheritance pattern
   • Recommend genetic counseling for extended family planning

REPORTED BY
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director

[redacted name], MD
Clinical Geneticist

clinical_context.referral_reason: 3-year-old female presenting with developmental regression, loss of purposeful hand skills, stereotypic hand movements, and acquired microcephaly. Clinical suspicion of Rett syndrome
clinical_context.test_clinical_rationale: Whole exome sequencing to identify genetic cause of neurodevelopmental regression and confirm suspected Rett syndrome diagnosis

clinical_findings.value: Normal development until approximately 18 months of age
Gradual loss of acquired language skills and purposeful hand use
Head circumference decelerated from 50th percentile at birth to below 3rd percentile
No family history of neurodevelopmental disorders

biomarker_test_results.test_methodology: Whole exome sequencing with trio analysis using Agilent SureSelect Human All Exon V7 library preparation on Illumina NovaSeq 6000
biomarker_test_results.result_description: Heterozygous nonsense variant detected in proband, not detected in either parent, confirming de novo status
biomarker_test_results.clinical_implications: Confirms classic Rett syndrome diagnosis. p.Arg270* is common MECP2 mutation accounting for ~6% of classic Rett syndrome cases, associated with typical clinical progression including regression, loss of hand skills, microcephaly, and variable seizure onset

clinical_outcome.overall_implications: De novo MECP2 p.Arg270* variant confirms Rett syndrome diagnosis. This variant typically presents with classic phenotype including regression phase stabilizing by age 4-5, preserved ambulation in 50%, communication limited to eye gaze, 70% seizure risk by adolescence, and increased scoliosis risk after age 8
clinical_outcome.overall_recommendations: Multidisciplinary care required: pediatric neurology for seizure monitoring, physical therapy for motor function, occupational therapy for hand function, speech/communication therapy with augmentative devices. Annual EEG monitoring, scoliosis screening after age 5, nutritional assessment, cardiac evaluation with QTc monitoring. Genetic counseling for ~1% parental recurrence risk due to possible germline mosaicism. Prenatal testing available for future pregnancies
